title: This first-of-a-kind agreement will set a new standard for safe and responsible AI use in schools. We are making these protections available to every school district in the US.
summary: This first-of-a-kind agreement will set a new standard for safe and responsible AI use in schools. We are making these protections available to every school district in the US. | 75 comments on LinkedIn
body_markdown: This is an important move in the right direction. What stands out most is the shift from broad AI principles toward enforceable protections around data use, human oversight, transparency, and institutional control. From the Roots Informatics perspective, the next step is to make those protections portable across the AI stack. Schools will not use one AI provider forever. They will use multiple models, applications, agents, analytics tools, and cloud environments. Governance should not have to be reinvented every time the vendor changes. That raises a larger infrastructure question: Who owns the rules—the school system, or the technology provider? Our view through Convergence is that the institution should retain control over: • who may access student data, • what purpose that data may serve, • which AI systems are authorized, • when human approval is required, • what actions an AI agent may take, • and what evidence must exist afterward. Microsoft should be able to comply with those rules. So should Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and the next generation of providers. The governance layer should belong to the institution, not disappear inside the application. This agreement helps define an important standard.
